facts.statement: The genus Diomedeoides was described by Fischer in 1985.
The type species of the genus is Diomedeoides minimus.
Fossils of Diomedeoides date from the Early Oligocene to the Early Miocene.
Diomedeoides is an extinct genus of seabirds.
facts.quote: Diomedeoides is a prehistoric genus of seabirds.

facts.statement: Diomedeoides belonged to the order Procellariiformes, which includes modern albatrosses and petrels.
facts.quote: The family was in the order Procellariiformes which today is composed of the albatrosses and petrels.

facts.statement: Diomedeoides is currently the only genus known in the family Diomedeoididae.
facts.quote: At present it is the only genus in the family Diomedeoididae.

facts.statement: Three species of Diomedeoides have been described.
Researchers suggest that Diomedeoides may be a junior synonym of the genus Rupelornis.
facts.quote: it is likely that the genus name Diomedeoides is actually a junior synonym of Rupelornis (van Beneden, 1871).

facts.statement: Fossils of Diomedeoides have been found in Oligocene and Miocene rocks in Europe and Iran.
facts.quote: Fossils of this genus have been found in the Oligocene and Miocene rocks in Europe and Iran.

facts.statement: Two species of Diomedeoides are known from Central Europe, while a third species is known only from Iran.
facts.quote: Two species, D. brodkorbi and D. lipsiensis, are known from Central Europe, and a third species, D. babaheydariensis, is known only from Iran.

facts.statement: The parent group of Diomedeoides is the family Procellariidae.
Diomedeoides lived between 33.9 and 23.04 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Rupelian to Chattian (33.9 to 23.04 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Diomedeoides is classified in the class Aves.
